summary.tldr: Creates a Criminal Code offence for wilfully promoting a terrorist activity or terrorist group, with a maximum penalty of five years.
what_it_does: Creates an indictable offence for anyone who, by communicating statements, wilfully promotes a terrorist activity, a terrorist group, or any activity of a terrorist group.
Sets the maximum penalty for this offence at five years in prison.
Says the offence can apply even if the statements do not specifically mention a terrorist activity or do not actually encourage anyone to take part.

Gives defences if the statements were true, were made in good faith on a religious subject, were on a matter of public interest believed to be true, or were made in good faith to point out material for removal.
Requires any sentence for this offence, other than life imprisonment, to be served after the sentences for the listed terrorism offences.
Adds the new offence to Criminal Code definitions used for terrorism offences and for section 183.
summary.background: The bill amends the Criminal Code. It adds a new section 83.171 and changes related definitions and sentencing rules.
